question: What specific named datasets were used to train this AI model? List only the dataset names.
keywords: training data dataset corpus fine-tuned trained on pre-trained pre-training data source
description: Per SPDX 3.0.1 trainedOn relationship: identifies the specific datasets used to train the AI model. The answer should list concrete dataset names (e.g. "SQuAD", "Common Crawl", "The Pile") rather than generic descriptions. Maps to SPDX trainedOn relationship and CycloneDX modelCard.datasets with type=training.

retrieval.hypothetical_passage: The model was pre-trained on a 1.5T-token mixture of Common Crawl (filtered with CCNet), C4, The Pile, Wikipedia, GitHub, ArXiv, and StackExchange. We then fine-tuned on the SQuAD v2 question-answering set and a small instruction-tuning corpus derived from FLAN. Dataset card links and per-source token counts are listed in the appendix; license terms for each constituent corpus are documented in DATA_LICENSES.md.

extraction.instruction: Extract the named datasets used to TRAIN (pre-train and/or fine-tune) this AI model. Return only the canonical dataset names, comma-separated. CRITICAL: do NOT include datasets that the model is merely evaluated/benchmarked on — those belong in testedOnDatasets, not here.
extraction.field_spec: AIkaBoOM-internal. Value space: a list of dataset names (canonical short forms preferred, e.g. `Common Crawl`, `C4`, `The Pile`, `SQuAD`). Maps to SPDX `trainedOn` relationship and CycloneDX `modelCard.datasets` with `type=training`.
extraction.output_guidance:
INCLUDE a dataset only if the source explicitly states it was used to TRAIN the model. Look for verbs like: 'trained on', 'pre-trained on', 'fine-tuned on', 'training corpus', 'training mixture', 'continued pretraining', 'distilled from'. Section markers that signal training: 'Training Data', 'Pretraining', 'Fine-tuning', 'Training Corpus'.

EXCLUDE any dataset that only appears in: evaluation/benchmark sections, results tables, 'Evaluation', 'Benchmarks', 'Test', 'Zero-shot evaluation', 'Linear probe', leaderboard tables, accuracy/F1/pass@1 score lists. A dataset listed under 'we evaluate on …' or appearing only with a numeric score in a results table is an evaluation dataset, NOT training data — even if it's well-known like SQuAD, GLUE, ImageNet, MMLU, HumanEval.

WORKED EXAMPLES:
• BERT paper says 'pre-trained on BookCorpus and English Wikipedia' AND lists GLUE/SQuAD scores in Table 1 → trainedOn = `BookCorpus, English Wikipedia` (NOT SQuAD, NOT GLUE).
• CLIP paper lists 30+ datasets in an evaluation table (Food101, CIFAR10, ImageNet, …) and says 'we trained on a dataset of 400 million (image, text) pairs collected from the internet' (often called WIT/YFCC100M-derived) → trainedOn = `WIT, YFCC100M` (or `400M image-text web pairs` if no name) — NOT the 30 evaluation datasets.
• If a paper says 'we report results on GLUE, SuperGLUE, MMLU' with no training-data sentence, return `noAssertion` — silence about training data is silence; do not pull from the evaluation list.

List concrete names only, preserve official capitalization, de-duplicate. Include BOTH pre-training and fine-tuning corpora when both are explicitly named. If training data is acknowledged but no dataset is named (e.g. 'proprietary internal data', 'a large web corpus'), or if training data is not discussed at all, return noAssertion.
